page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.xlarge is an arm64-based virtual machine instance powered by the custom Alibaba YiTian710 processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores with a clock speed of 2.75 GHz and no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 64 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several standard operations. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1819.58 and a multi-core score of 7234.41. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block speed of 409.68 GB/sec, though large block write bandwidth is weaker at 24.45 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are solid, with Redis SET operations reaching 6.4 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 6.29 GB/sec. However, cryptographic performance is poor, as shown by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 654.15.

From a resource-density perspective, the custom Arm-based architecture offers a highly cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive applications that do not require x86-specific instruction sets. The dedicated core allocation ensures predictable compute performance. However, users must consider tradeoffs, such as the lack of local NVMe storage and weak performance in complex vector or cryptographic calculations, as evidenced by the low Passmark CPU scores. Large-scale LLM inference is also limited, with 7B model text generation performing poorly at 4.59 tokens per second.

This instance is well-suited for memory-bound workloads that benefit from dedicated Arm cores. Appropriate use cases include medium-sized in-memory databases like Redis, caching layers, static web serving, and general-purpose data processing pipelines that fit within the 32 GB memory envelope.
